turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Liew, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your knee surgery today. Let's go through some questions to make sure everything's in order, okay?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Morning, doctor. Yes, sure thing. I'm ready when you are.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Great. First, can you tell me a bit about your knee problem? How long have you been having issues with it?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Oh, about five years already. The pain got worse last year, can't even walk properly now. That's why I'm doing this surgery, right?

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Understood. Now, let's go through your medications. You're on amlodipine for blood pressure, metformin and glipizide for diabetes, atorvastatin for cholesterol, omeprazole for stomach, and aspirin which was stopped recently?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, that's all correct. I take them every day except the aspirin, which I stopped a week ago like the doctor told me.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good. Any allergies to medications or other things?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Hmm, I don't think so. The records say no allergies, right?

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Actually, I noticed the records say 'no known allergies,' but sometimes people might not mention things they think aren't important. Have you ever had a reaction to any medications, especially sulfa antibiotics?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Oh! Wait a minute... I had a rash once from some antibiotic. Was it sulfa? I think so. The doctor said it was an allergy, so I stopped taking that type since.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you for mentioning that. So, a rash reaction to sulfa antibiotics. We'll make sure to note that properly. Any other reactions?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, that's the only one. I don't react to anything else.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Excellent. Have you eaten or drunk anything since midnight? We need to confirm you're NPO for surgery.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, nothing since last night dinner. Just water for meds this morning, but that was hours ago.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Perfect. Any previous anesthesia or surgeries?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Only once, a cataract surgery years ago. They gave me local anesthesia, I think. No problems then.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good to know. Lastly, how's your mobility before surgery? Can you walk with assistance?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, with a walking stick. But the pain makes it hard, so I don't go out much now.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you, Mr. Tan. We'll proceed with spinal anesthesia as planned, with general as backup. I'll see you in the operating room shortly.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Alright, doctor. Thank you for explaining everything.
